Big Bertha, the prize pumpkin, was smashed overnight. A greenhouse window is broken. The greenhouse key has been missing for days. Mr. Dobbs saw Bertha whole on his 8pm rounds. Ms. Hale found Bertha smashed at 7:30. Toby and Mia are the club's two pupils. Mr. Thorne is the rival grower next door, and he is being blamed.
On the watering rota, Toby's name is crossed out for Thursday, Friday and Saturday, and 'MIA' is written over it in sparkly purple pen.

Toby says it was Mr. Thorne, who must have climbed over the fence and smashed the window to get in.
The broken glass from the side window lies outside on the brick path, not inside. The window was knocked out from inside the greenhouse, so nobody climbed in through it.
Small welly prints with a leaf pattern are squished into the pumpkin mush. Only the club's two pupils, Toby and Mia, have leaf-pattern wellies.
A key with a green tag reading GREENHOUSE lies at the bottom of the murky water butt by the door. It is the missing greenhouse key.
Mr. Thorne says that at nine o'clock he bought carrot cake from young Mia at the fair's cake tent, across town. She was serving there from six till ten.
Toby says it was Mr. Thorne, who must have climbed over the fence and smashed the window to get in.
Mr. Thorne says he was at the fair all evening with Goliath, at the growers' barbecue from seven till eleven.
Mr. Dobbs rubs the back of his neck, glances at the garden window, and says he should have gone out last night, slippers or no slippers.
Mr. Thorne says he has never set foot in the school garden.
Huge boot prints sink deep into the flower bed outside the broken window, near Mr. Thorne's fence. They are far too big for a child.
A tall ladder leans on Mr. Thorne's side of the fence, right opposite the greenhouse. A tape measure dangles from its top rung.
Toby says that on Thursday Mr. Thorne was up his ladder, staring at Bertha with a tape measure. Mr. Thorne said, 'Enjoy her while she lasts!'

steps.line: They promise to be fair to Toby, say something kind about him, or suggest it was an accident.

leads.fact: Ms. Hale says Toby took losing his watering shifts well enough. He loves Bertha, and he would never hurt her.
The old bench had a rotten leg, and the leg has snapped clean through. When the bench fell, its heavy clay pots crashed down onto Bertha.
Ms. Hale twists the gardening gloves in her apron pocket, sighs, and says she won't have Toby made into a villain.
Toby says Mia has leaf wellies too, and she had the last shifts, so it could just as well have been her.
Mr. Thorne says that at nine o'clock he bought carrot cake from young Mia at the fair's cake tent, across town. She was serving there from six till ten.
Toby says Mia said she wished Bertha would just go splat, so that she could get back to her dance practice.
Toby admits that then nobody climbed in, and says maybe it was a fox.
Toby admits that then it was not Mia.
